14765181.note:
City of Ocean Shores, zoned R1. Parcel 094100903600, 9,104 sq ft. County land value $22,550 vs $25,000 ask; last sold $29,900 in 2005. City water, sewer and power in the street; listing says LIDs paid in full. Taxes about $141/yr, no HOA.

LiDAR (USGS 3DEP, 2019): basically flat, 2.8% overall, falling gently NE. Small dune hummocks. Ground only 10-15 ft above sea level.

RV: up to 120 cumulative days a year on a 'semideveloped' lot (code says a vacant lot 'with power, water and sewer'), 90 days on an undeveloped lot. The cap is per person across every lot you own in the city. Up to 2 RVs, free online camping permit before each placement, self-contained or hooked to sewer (no porta-potty). An RV parked after 10 p.m. counts as a day. Tent only alongside an RV, max 100 sq ft. With a building permit, 6 months of RV living during construction, once per person ever. No renting the lot.

Short-term rentals: only in B-1 and B-2 zones, not R1. Trees and grading: clearing vegetation or grading needs a city clearing and grading permit; removing soil below 18 in above road centerline needs a conditional use permit.

Shed with no house: one shed up to 120 sq ft ($75 nonaccessory structure application), no power or plumbing, 5 ft from side and rear lines. Tiny house on wheels counts as an RV even if hooked up. An L&I-insignia factory-built tiny home on a foundation should count as a house (modular homes are treated as site-built). Hookup fees from city code: about $3.4K-6.4K for water and sewer.

Hazards: FEMA Zone X. A mapped freshwater marsh (NWI) is about 30 ft from the lot line, which can trigger the city's wetland review and buffer. Whole town is in the Cascadia tsunami zone (2018 state models).

Suggested offer: open $18-19K, aim for $20-22K, with a 30-day feasibility period for the wetland buffer.

sources.title: KNKX: new SW Washington tsunami maps

195117826.note:
Unincorporated Pacific County, zoned R-R. Parcel 74067004006: two platted lots, about 22,700 sq ft total. County land value $20,000 vs $25,000 ask; most of the block is $10K vacant lots. Zillow's map pin is on the wrong lot (3100 102nd St). Power in the street; no sewer, no water.

LiDAR (2019): dead flat, 0.2%, 12-15 ft above sea level.

The problem: the federal wetland map (NWI) puts about 98% of the lot inside a 14-acre forested wetland, with 31- and 43-acre wetlands within about 60 ft. Soil is Seastrand mucky peat, very poorly drained, with the wet-season water table about 6 in down; septic rated very limited. County wetland code (Ord. 193) gives interdunal wetlands over 1 acre buffers of 75-300 ft, so the only path is a reasonable use exception: about 3,000 sq ft of disturbance for house, septic and landscaping plus a driveway up to 600 sq ft, with a paid critical-area report and mitigation plan.

RV (Ord. 194): one RV at a time, kept licensed and movable, never a permanent dwelling. More than 7 days in a row or 30 days a year needs sewer or approved septic, which can be waived with pumper or dump-station receipts. Up to 1 year during construction with an active building permit. Tents banned on vacant R-R lots except with temporary RV use. One temporary shed up to 120 sq ft. Short-term rentals allowed in R-R with conditions.

Verdict: pass, or worth it only under about $10K as an RV-and-dump-station camp spot.

sources.title: Pacific County ordinances (Ord. 193 critical areas, Ord. 194 zoning)

203503596.note:
Unincorporated Grays Harbor County, zoned R-3 Resort Residential (listing's 'Jurisdiction: City' is wrong). Parcel 750507100000, 6,098 sq ft corner lot in Haven by the Sea. County land value $40,171 vs $25,999 ask (cut from $31,999 on 8/27/2026). Water and power in the street, no sewer.

LiDAR (2009): flat, 1.1%, 15-18 ft above sea level. No mapped wetland on the lot (nearest pond about 375 ft). FEMA Zone X.

RV: county code 8.20 authorizes 2 RVs or other camping on a private lot when it has sanitary facilities approved by the health authority. The county RV brochure says full-time RV living is OK with an approved septic (2-bedroom minimum) and legal water. Before septic: 14 consecutive days within any 2-month period, self-contained or serviced porta-potty, keep dump receipts. No renting the RV; covers, decks and sheds need permits.

House allowed outright; the lot is under the 7,200 sq ft minimum but code 17.72.070 treats a lot of record as conforming. Short-term rentals are a permitted use in R-3 with an annual county STR permit. No county tree-cutting permit found in zoning.

Septic is make-or-break: Yaquina loamy fine sand, somewhat poorly drained, wet-season water table about 12 in, rated very limited. State rules want 13,000+ sq ft on public water; smaller lots of record qualify only if the design meets every rule with no waivers. Corner lot means 25 ft front setbacks on both streets, so house plus drainfield must fit in roughly 25 x 65 ft. Ask for the Haven by the Sea CC&Rs. Likely in the Cascadia tsunami zone (not confirmed for this lot).

Suggested offer: open about $20K, aim for $22-24K, contingent on a septic designer's soil evaluation.

196138962.note:
Unincorporated Pacific County, zoned R-R (per the state's prototype zoning atlas; confirm). Parcel 75015010011: two 50 x 100 ft lots plus 30 ft of road. County land value $60,000 vs $29,900 ask. On market since 6/2025; went pending Jan 2026 and fell through. Taxes about $492/yr. Power in the street; no sewer, no water.

LiDAR (2009/2019): not 'mostly level'. Overall 6% falling NW, but a dune trough about 10 ft deep runs N-S through the west-middle; median local slope 19%, some spots 30-45%. Elevation 19-31 ft. Flattest building ground is the east ridge (about 29-31 ft) and the south end.

Soil: Netarts fine sand, well drained, no water table found; septic rated very limited because sand drains fast (usually solvable with pressure distribution). Nearest wetland about 525 ft away, beyond the largest 300 ft county buffer. FEMA Zone X. Tsunami not confirmed.

Zoning (Ord. 194): one house per lot of record, or two houses or a duplex. Old lots are exempt from the current minimum lot size. RV: one at a time, licensed and movable, not a permanent dwelling; more than 7 days in a row or 30 days a year needs septic unless waived with pumper or dump receipts; up to 1 year during construction with a building permit. Tent only alongside temporary RV use. One temporary shed up to 120 sq ft. Short-term rentals allowed in R-R but must be 300 ft from any other vacation rental (no variance), with posted and mailed notice, parking for each bedroom (2 minimum) and a septic inspection. No tree or clearing permit found in county zoning.

Make-or-break: state rules require 100 ft between a drainfield and any well, including neighbors'. On 100 x 100 ft that likely means well and drainfield in opposite corners, depending on neighbors' systems.

Suggested offer: open about $22K, aim for $24-26K, contingent on a septic designer's site plan showing well and drainfield fit.

tags: No RV or tent without a house
200115486.note: City of Newport. Asking $37,500; the county codes the lot 'unbuildable' with a real market value of $1,050. No tent or RV living without a house (Newport code 14.16.020(B) and 14.06.050). Trees fall under the geologic hazard exemption: under 8 in diameter is free, and no more than 25% of the canopy per year.

198986077.note:
City of Lincoln City, zoned RM. Asking $35,000. LiDAR: 35% average slope, with a level bench mid-lot. Building permits about $2.5-2.9K; system development charges and hookups about $20K. No short-term rentals in RM. Trees 6 in and larger need a permit.

Suggested offer: open $26K, target $29-31K.

134333814.note:
Unincorporated Lincoln County, zoned R-1, inside the Toledo urban growth boundary. About 2 acres under 20% slope. No county tree permit. RV allowed only during construction (1 year). Can't partition (5-acre minimum inside the growth boundary). Excavating or filling is a conditional use in R-1.

Georgia-Pacific kraft mill is about 1.5 mi south; Oregon DEQ fined it $116K in 2025. Wetlands 457-720 ft away. Soil has bedrock at 20-60 in; septic rated very limited.

183463933.note:
Unincorporated Tillamook County, Pacific City/Woods, zoned PCW-R2 (medium-density residential). Tax lot 4S1030AA00200, about 60,000 sq ft (1.38 acres). Listed $175,000, 123 days on market, last sold Feb 2023; owner lives in Valley Center, CA. Listing says public water, septic needed. County assessed value not checked (assessor site blocked automated reads).

LiDAR (USGS 3DEP, 2009): not a level lot. Overall 29% slope falling SE (bearing 134) toward the river; local slope median 33%, 90th percentile 58%, max 72%. Elevation 51-135 ft. The only gentle ground is the top (north) edge at about 123-134 ft, roughly a 100 x 60 ft bench; everything below drops steeply. Building and drainfield would have to share that bench.

Hazards: FEMA Zone X. No mapped wetland on the lot; tidal Nestucca River (NWI riverine) about 160 ft away, small seasonal creeks about 130 ft away (county riparian setback along the Nestucca is 50 ft). DOGAMI SLIDO shows a prehistoric shallow earth-flow landslide nearby but not touching the lot. Outside the tsunami zone, even the largest (XXL) Cascadia scenario on DOGAMI's maps.

Soil: Fendall-Munsoncreek complex (SSURGO map unit 121D, about 18% typical slope, capability class 6e: erosion-limited). The USDA septic rating couldn't be pulled (soil database was down); slope alone makes septic hard here.

Rules: PCW-R2 allows one- or two-family dwellings outright and lists temporary construction trailers or RVs as an outright use. County LUO 5.010 requires a placement permit before any RV goes on a lot; during construction the RV must be unhooked and stored or removed within 30 days after the building permit closes. Living in an RV on the vacant lot without a building permit was not found as allowed; a 2018 LUBA ruling read county code as limiting RVs to non-residential vacation use. The zone's stated purpose assumes public sewer, which this lot lacks.

Short-term rentals: county STR license cap. West of the Nestucca (Alder St south to Bob Straub) is cap-free since Jan 2025; the rest of Pacific City/Woods is capped at 95 licenses. This lot sits inside a river bend, so which side it falls on isn't confirmed.

Verdict: a view lot, not a camp spot. Make-or-break is fitting house plus septic on the small north bench of a 29% slope, near an old landslide. Suggested offer: open about $140K, aim $150-155K, contingent on a septic site evaluation and a geotechnical look at the slope.

sources.title: LUBA: Oregon Coast Reliance v. Tillamook County (2018)
Headlight Herald: STR cap-exempt zone in Pacific City

134130041.note:
Unincorporated Lincoln County near Seal Rock. Tax lot 12-11-30-CC-00301-00, 3.5 acres; owner in Toledo, OR. Listed $260,000, 178 days on market; Zestimate $243,200. Agent Matt Moore, Elkhorn Real Estate. Already has public water, power and a 4-bedroom septic installed in 2002; phone and cable available. The old manufactured home on it has no value per the listing (removal cost is on the buyer). Zoning and county assessed value not confirmed (Lincoln County's property and map sites need in-page searches).

LiDAR (USGS 3DEP, 2009): overall 5% falling north, but not uniform. The east half is a flat pasture at about 111-118 ft; the west end is a treed rise up to about 125 ft. A seasonal creek ravine runs north-south through the middle, 25-35 ft deep (down to about 77 ft), with sides up to 40-56% slope. Local slope median 15%. Plenty of flat building ground on the east side.

Hazards: FEMA Zone X. Outside the tsunami zone, even the largest (XXL) Cascadia scenario on DOGAMI's maps. No NWI wetland on the lot (nearest riverine wetland about 600 ft); the unnamed seasonal creek is mapped in NHD and likely brings a riparian setback along the ravine. DOGAMI SLIDO shows a historic (under 150 years) shallow slide nearby, not on the lot. Soil: Nelscott (SSURGO map unit 64692); USDA septic rating not pulled (soil database down), but the existing approved 4-bedroom system makes that less critical.

RV and rules: Lincoln County RV and camping rules for this zone not yet confirmed. On the Toledo lot (Lincoln County R-1), RVs were allowed only during construction (1 year).

Verdict: one of the more usable lots so far: flat, utilities and septic already in, half a mile from the ocean. Make-or-break: confirm zoning and RV rules, have the 2002 septic inspected, and price in removing the manufactured home. Suggested offer: open about $225K, aim $235-245K, contingent on septic inspection.

areas.note: City of Ocean Shores (code chapter 15.12): RV camping on a vacant lot is capped at 90 days a year, or 120 days on a 'semideveloped' lot with power, water and sewer. The cap is per person across every lot you own in the city. Up to 2 RVs, free online camping permit before each placement, self-contained or hooked to sewer. Tent only with an RV. 6 months in an RV during construction with a building permit, once per person ever. Short-term rentals only in B-1 and B-2 zones. One shed up to 120 sq ft allowed on a vacant lot ($75 application, no power or plumbing).

Unincorporated Grays Harbor County (code 8.20): up to 2 RVs or other camping on a private lot once it has health-approved sanitary facilities; the county brochure says full-time RV living is OK with an approved 2-bedroom septic and legal water. Without septic: 14 consecutive days within any 2-month period. Short-term rentals allowed with an annual county permit in G-1, G-5, R-2, R-3, RR, LQ and C-2.

Unincorporated Pacific County (Ord. 194, section 21.I): one RV at a time, kept licensed and movable, never a permanent dwelling. More than 7 days in a row or 30 days a year needs sewer or approved septic, waivable with pumper or dump-station receipts. Up to 1 year during construction with an active building permit. Tents banned on vacant lots in R-1, R-2, R-3, R-R, MU and C-C except with temporary RV use. New vacation rentals are prohibited in R-1; in R-2 and R-R they must be 300 ft from any other vacation rental.

City of Newport (NMC 14.06.050): RVs may be stored but not lived in, except in a manufactured dwelling park, an RV park, or as temporary living quarters authorized under NMC chapter 14.9. Taking the wheels off or setting an RV on a foundation doesn't change that. An RV can only discharge wastewater into public sewer or an approved septic. RV parks are only allowed as a conditional use in R-4 (and publicly owned P-1/P-2). Accessory structures like sheds follow the same rules as the primary use (NMC 14.16.020).

City of Lincoln City: cutting trees 6 in diameter or larger needs a city tree permit. Short-term rentals are not allowed in the RM zone. On the TL5300 NE 27th Dr lot, building permits ran about $2.5-2.9K and system development charges plus hookups about $20K.

City of Cannon Beach: cutting trees needs a city permit, and trees cut inside a wetland buffer must be left on site. Wetland plus its 50 ft buffer can cover most of a lot; a lot of record that is mostly wetland was limited to about 1,000 sq ft of building coverage plus 400 sq ft of other coverage on the lot researched. Short-term rental permits are capped with a waitlist; the waitlist starts 11/5/2026.
